caption: R4 500 for one night because she asked and I said yes. Would you have done the same?

slides.title:
How I'm paying for
my daughter's matric dance
on R19 400 p/m
Living in Thabazimbi
slides.body:
Female, 45
Single mother, daughter (18) in matric
Job: Enrolled nursing assistant, provincial clinic
Net salary: R19 400 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: We've been in the same house for nine years. My daughter's friends all know where the spare key is.

slides.title: Matric dance
slides.includes: Dress R2 200, hair and makeup R900, shoes R600, ticket R800
slides.body: The ticket alone was R800. I said yes before I looked at the list.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: For two, with a teenager who is always hungry
slides.body: She eats the way I did at her age. I just didn't have anyone to buy it.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My mother in Mokopane, my younger brother's rent
slides.body: He's looking for work. I've stopped asking how long he'll be looking.

slides.title: School costs
slides.includes: Matric jacket, final exam fees, photos, stationery
slides.body: There is always one more form with an amount on it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, funeral policy, burial society, stokvel, phone, transport to the clinic
slides.body: The stokvel pays out in December. I've already promised it to three things.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R19 400. The dance was R4 500 on top of a normal month. I paid it from what was left and a little from December.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it grouped the dance spending into one picture.

I hadn't added up the dress, the hair and the shoes together.

No bank login needed.
